author: fester
body: This was a BINARY search until 2026-07-28, and it silently found only some of its names. A binary search requires the list to be ordered by the same comparison it searches with, and the two disagreed: the list is written in alphabetical order, while `text-compare` orders by CCE code point, and CCE numbers letters by FREQUENCY. `c` is 24 and `b` is 32, so `char-at` sorts before `bit-and` under the comparator and after it in the list. Names past the first such inversion were unreachable, and an unreachable builtin does not fail loudly: it falls through to the ordinary apply path and emits a call to a subprogram Ada has never heard of.

author: fester
body: A linear scan has no ordering invariant to get wrong, and this runs once per call site at transpile time.
